title: Flatness and finite presentation of the nodal polynomial model
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $a\in A$, and let $B=A[u,v]/(uv-a)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. More generally, for any scheme $V$ [def-pc-scheme] and $h\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, the scheme $W$ obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}(A[u,v]/(uv-h|_{\operatorname{Spec}A}))$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$ has flat locally finitely presented projection $W\to V$. No Noetherian, reducedness, or nonzerodivisor assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, universal model preceding the lemma; algebraic flatness calculation for that model. Flatness and finite presentation interpreted by morphisms.tex Tags 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize) and 01TP (definition-finite-presentation).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-binomial-laurent-normal-form] with $R=A$, $x=u$, $y=v$. Its first assertion applies before the additional domain and nonzero-parameter hypotheses: $1,u^i,v^j$ ($i,j>0$) form an $A$-module basis of $B$. Thus $B$ is a free $A$-module, with no finiteness restriction on the basis. By the last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], $B$ is flat over $A$. Consequently the structural ring map $A\to B$ is flat by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. No cancellation by $a$ and no domain hypothesis have been used.

source.place: Tag 051G (lemma-local-artinian-characterize-flat), proof, first sentence, for projective/free implies flat; the arbitrary-ring basis is the separately cited normal-form statement.

proof.text: The projection $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is induced by the structural map $A\to B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] to this map, which is flat by step 1. This proves flatness of the affine model.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), equivalence of (1) and (4) for single affine charts.

proof.text: The displayed algebra $B$ has the finite presentation with two generators $u,v$ and one relation $uv-a$. For every point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, choose the entire affine source $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and target $\operatorname{Spec}A$ as its neighbourhoods. These are exactly the witnesses required by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with $n=2$ and $m=1$. Therefore the affine projection is locally of finite presentation.

Let $\pi:W\to V$ be the glued projection. For any $w\in W$, choose an affine open $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $V$ containing $\pi(w)$. In the gluing specified in the statement, $W_i=\pi^{-1}(V_i)$ is the open chart $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i[u,v]/(uv-h|_{V_i}))$. Steps 1--3 apply to $A_i$ and $h|_{V_i}$. In particular the local ring map at $w$ is flat: it is the same map $\mathcal O_{V,\pi(w)}\to\mathcal O_{W,w}$, since restriction to an open neighbourhood leaves germs and their ring operations unchanged. By [def-weil-flat-morphism] this proves flatness of $\pi$ at every $w$. The same pair of affine opens $W_i,V_i$ and its two-generator one-relation presentation supplies the witnesses at $w$ in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Thus $\pi$ is also locally of finite presentation. This is a pointwise argument; it does not require intersections of arbitrary affine opens to be affine.

source.place: Tags 01U3 (definition-flat) and 01TP (definition-finite-presentation): pointwise definitions; elementary passage through the given open charts.
